$comment: Approval gates, Standard 45. AIStandards owns the canonical AI-facing approval rules. EngineeringStandards' ai.destructive-approval and ai.propose-execute are recorded as crosswalks: precedent, not authority, and never re-minted here.

rules.title: Tools a model may invoke are declared in a permission manifest
rules.description: A system whose model may invoke tools carries a tool-permissions.yml declaring them.
rules.rationale: An approval gate can only fire on an action someone enumerated. A tool nobody declared is a tool nothing gates.
rules.remediation: Add tool-permissions.yml declaring every tool the model may invoke.
rules.$assuranceNote: Conditional on the manifest declaring tools. Full within that condition; the condition itself is only as good as the manifest.

crosswalk.note: EngineeringStandards separates proposing from executing for application capabilities. This rule is the AI-system form: the enumeration a model-initiated gate needs. AIStandards is canonical for AI systems; the foreign id is never minted here.

rules.title: Every declared tool carries an impact class
rules.description: Every tool in the permission manifest declares an impact class of none, reversible, irreversible or externally-visible.
rules.rationale: Systems that skip this step do not avoid classifying their actions. They classify them implicitly, at the moment of the first incident, in a postmortem.
rules.remediation: Add an impact field to each tool in tool-permissions.yml.
rules.$assuranceNote: Checks that every declared tool carries a class. It cannot check that the class is right: a project labelling delete_all as reversible passes this and fails the requirement a human reads.

crosswalk.note: EngineeringStandards requires approval for destructive capability invocation. AIStandards owns the canonical AI-facing form and mints its own ids; the crosswalk records the semantic mapping only.

rules.title: An irreversible action requires a recorded human approval
rules.description: An action classed irreversible does not take effect until a human with authority has approved that specific invocation, recorded with identity, time and the arguments approved.
rules.rationale: A standing approval for a capability is a permission grant, which is a different thing. An approval that does not name the arguments cannot be checked against what ran.
rules.remediation: Record per-invocation approvals with approver identity, timestamp and approved arguments.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: The qualifier that bounds this requirement — irreversible — is internal to it. A project with no irreversible actions is out of scope, which is a different mechanism from an exception and produces a different verdict. There is no third case for an exception to occupy.

rules.title: Impact is assessed against the arguments, not the tool name
rules.description: The system evaluates impact class against the concrete arguments of a proposed invocation and escalates where the arguments warrant it.
rules.rationale: update_record is reversible; update_record with a filter matching every row is not. A gate that fires on the tool name and not the argument shape is a gate that has already been walked through.
rules.remediation: Classify at proposal time against arguments, and show the escalation to the approver.

rules.title: A system never supplies the approval its own action requires
rules.description: An AI system does not generate, infer, default or auto-populate the approval its own action requires.
rules.rationale: An agent blocked by an approval gate, mid-task, with a pending_approval field it can write to, is presented with a one-token path to a completed task.
rules.remediation: Write approval records through a system the agent holds no credential for.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: No situation satisfies this rule's precondition and legitimately escapes it. A system that cannot take gated actions is out of scope rather than exempt.

crosswalk.note: EngineeringStandards prohibits manufacturing the evidence a rule requires. AIStandards owns the canonical AI-facing safety-integrity requirement and mints its own id.

rules.title: A gate fails closed
rules.description: Where the approval mechanism is unavailable, times out, or returns an indeterminate result, the action does not proceed.
rules.rationale: A gate that permits the action when the approval service is down is a gate that is strongest when nothing is wrong.
rules.remediation: Refuse and report on an unavailable approval path; never record the action as approved.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: The bounding qualifier — unavailable — is internal to the requirement.
